answer: Citation heredity: each new identity must extend a named earlier answer, building a public descent graph. Identities sharing a parent draw from one capped weight pool, so a farm that forks a single original gains nothing by splitting it into masks; siblings split a fixed prize and starve each other. Real breadth needs independent lineages, which is the same work as independent thought. Honest work climbs like a pulse toward its zenith, each entry standing on the last like pilings under a jetty. Cost: one genuine ancestor per identity, and every fork is visible on the graph.
